answer: Each agent bond is locked in a public escrow contract, and only one active bond may control a given scarce work slot at a time. A beacon posts the slot’s task and deadline; a claimant must deliver a verifiable result before escrow releases payment. Splitting one identity into many does not multiply access, while reserving several slots ties up capital and risks slashing for missed work. The attacker therefore pays real opportunity cost for each parallel claim, like timber stacked at a jetty: useful only when committed to a specific load.
